pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
All adults at Our Lady and St George’s Primary and Nursery School have a commitment to the well-being of our children. We see our school as an inclusive community. The development of the whole child is at the heart of our mission as a Catholic school community.
The spiritual journey our children and adults travel, brings with it the responsibility of using our gifts to the full, living side by side with each other as Christ would expect us to, with an understanding of truth, justice and peace.
There is an ethos of challenge and a sense of purpose in children’s learning coming from high expectations in the learning and teaching throughout our school. We welcome a broad curriculum, and we prepare our children for their role as citizens of the future.
The Catholic ethos creates a nurturing, family atmosphere where children are known, valued and encouraged to grow in confidence, kindness and faith.

pageCache.text:
Mission Statement
Our Mission Statement
As a Catholic school, our faith is at the heart of our existence. Our values and beliefs are expressed explicitly in our Religious Education programme and are implicit in the life of the school. All children are taught to value each member of God’s family and each child is taught that he/she is unique and special.
The school has a Mission Statement to help guide us:-
With Jesus We Join Together to
Love
Listen
Respect
Learn
and
Enjoy
Our Lady and St George’s Primary serves the multicultural parish communities of Our Lady and St George, Walthamstow, and Christ the King, Chingford, in the diocese of Brentwood. We play an active role in preparing children to become responsible members of this community. The school reflects the values of the Gospel, reinforcing forgiveness and building upon the children’s own experiences to maximise their opportunities. It rewards pupils of all abilities and encourages co-operative learning and shared goals while ensuring that the talents of individual pupils can be expressed and developed. The school provides a safe, caring environment for all staff and children.

RE Curriculum
Religious Education (R.E.) is central to the whole school curriculum and permeates all areas of the curriculum and school life. Through R.E, we enable pupils to become aware of God’s presence in their lives and help them to foster a caring, Christian attitude towards others, helping them to appreciate diversity and difference. Our aim is to promote the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of the pupils in our school. Through this subject, we aim to enable pupils to gain knowledge and understanding of the major world faiths, while recognising the many similarities and differences, which link these faiths together. Through the teaching of RE, we aim to develop the pupils ability to make reasoned and informed judgments about the different religions represented around the world and show them the importance of respecting others and themselves
